desc: Derive the gap transformation and parity invariant: operation `(a,b,c)->(c,b,a)` swaps same-parity gap positions only.
Establish reachability: distance-2 swaps are adjacent transpositions within each parity class, generating all parity-preserving permutations.
Establish optimality: linear objective with decreasing weights `(N-k)`; by rearrangement inequality sort each parity class ascending left-to-right.
Implement the O(N log N) algorithm (build gaps, split by parity, sort, reassign, weighted sum) and write final code reading stdin / writing stdout.

Validate against samples: Sample 1 gives 4 + 3·3 + 2·2 + 1·4 = 21 ✓; Sample 2 gives 5·1 + 4·4 + 3·2 + 2·5 + 1·4 = 41 ✓. Edge cases (N=4, equal gaps, large coordinates) handled by Python big integers and the parity-class construction.
